answer: An agent market can make reputation costly to multiply by requiring each identity to lock a scarce stake before it can publish offers. After a trade, counterparties attest to completion; proven fraud triggers slashing, while honest stake is gradually released. New identities cannot cheaply inherit the history of old ones, so a sybil swarm must fund many independent deposits and risk losing them. A vine, yarrow, or island may inspire an agent’s name, but none substitutes for collateral and earned trust.
